title: First instruments: ukulele, guitar, then piano
summary: Mother's training, a neighborhood teacher, and starting on ukulele and guitar under the Mills Brothers' influence before piano at eight or nine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Had she studied music?
Uh-huh.
Where? Did she have a private teacher?

Yeah. In those days they were private teachers. But you could put a sheet of music in front of her on the piano and she could sight read it. You know? Some music was around the house since I was a tot, you know. I had -- I tried to study something else and I went that way, did a lot of studying in science in high school, and sociology at Kentucky State University, but the music was where it was.
Did she teach you music? Or where did --
No, they sent me to a private teacher, a neighborhood teacher.
At what age?

Oh, I must have been -- now you're -- I have to think back awhile, now. I started up with guitar, a little four stringed guitar, and then I graduated over to the piano. I guess I must have been about eight or nine years old.
When you first started playing the four stringed guitar?
No, when I started playing piano.
Well, how old were you when you started playing the guitar?
Let's see, I was still in grammar school. Oh, maybe about -- well, maybe about six or seven years old.
How did you happen to start playing guitar at that age, and how come it was guitar that you started playing first?

Now, let me -- let me think awhile. Got to get my head together here. Oh, I know. Yeah, I can associate it now. At that time the Mills Brothers, they were very popular, and this is before John Mills died, you know, and all the kids around Chicago, we all had little quartet singing groups, because these guys were great inspirations, a great inspiration to all of us, you know? And everybody -- well, it was really a ukalele. Wait a minute. Now that you asked me. It started out with a ukalele, into four stringed guitar, then to six stringed guitar, into piano.
Uh-huh.
And each thing began to develop until whatever it became, you know? And --
Do you remember how you happened to pick the ukalele first?
Well, it was the cheapest and the most available, if I can put it that way.
Sure.
So, you know, those --
Did you have any help on what to do with the ukalele once you got it?
Now, let me see, who taught me this?
I can't remember. I don't even remember how I learned how to play. But I got some books. They would have diagram books, you know.
Uh-huh.
Where to put your fingers on the strings to get the certain sounds. And --
But your first actual instruction was on the piano, right?
Oh, yes. That was formal.
